summary: Costa Rica's visa directives put nationals of countries including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, EU states, Australia and Japan in the first group, which enters without a visa for up to 180 days, and list as entry requirements proof of economic means of at least USD 100 per month or part of a month of stay and a return or onward ticket. Nationals of countries that need a consular visa may enter without it if they hold a multiple-entry visa or residence of the United States or Canada, a residence of the United Kingdom, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland or an EU country, or a multiple-entry Schengen C or D visa.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Costa Rica?
faq.answer: No. Costa Rica's visa directives put the United States in the first group, which enters without a visa for up to 180 days, with a minimum passport validity of one day; the stay granted by the immigration officer will not run beyond the passport's validity. The entry requirements include proof of economic means of at least USD 100 per month or part of a month of stay and a return or onward ticket.

faq.question: How long can tourists stay in Costa Rica?
faq.answer: Costa Rica's visa directives say first-group nationals (including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, EU states and Japan) can stay up to 180 days and second-group nationals up to 30 days, extendable to a total of 90 days; the immigration officer at entry decides the stay granted.

faq.question: Can I enter Costa Rica with a US or Schengen visa instead of a Costa Rican visa?
faq.answer: Yes, if you hold one of the documents Costa Rica's visa directives accept: a multiple-entry visa or residence of the United States or Canada valid for at least 1 day (US C1, C2 and C3 transit visas are not accepted), a residence of the United Kingdom, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland or an EU country that allows multiple entries or is valid for at least 90 days, or a multiple-entry Schengen C or D visa. With a US or Canadian visa or residence, the stay granted will not run beyond its validity.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Costa Rica?
faq.answer: Only if you come from a country on Costa Rica's list of countries with active yellow fever transmission: in the Americas Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, French Guiana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Venezuela and Trinidad and Tobago, plus the African countries on the same list. Costa Rica's health ministry says vaccination is mandatory at least 10 days before entry for anyone coming from those countries.

faq.question: Do I have to pay a departure tax when leaving Costa Rica?
faq.answer: The UK government says that when leaving by air you may need to pay a departure tax of USD 29, that most airlines include it in the ticket price, and that if you have to pay it you can use cash or card. No official source we could read states the tax for leaving overland.
